content: The hum of servers filled the cavernous data center like a chorus of mechanical whispers, their blinking lights casting long shadows across the cold, sterile floor. Detective Harlan Voss adjusted his rumpled trench coat, the weight of too many late nights pressing down on him as he stepped over a tangle of cables, each one a potential lead—or a trap. The air smelled of ozone and burnt coffee, the kind that had been sitting too long in the break room. A lone technician, pale under the fluorescent glow, glanced up from his terminal, fingers hovering over the keys like a man afraid of what he might uncover. "You shouldn’t be here," he muttered, but Voss just lit a cigarette, the smoke curling around the fire suppression sensors. "Neither should you," he replied, eyeing the flickering screen where a single line of code pulsed like a dying heartbeat. Somewhere in this labyrinth of data, a secret was bleeding out—and Voss was the only one who could stop the hemorrhage.
